prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth strip places the garage floor and nearby clutter in the bright foreground, with shelving, walls, and the back of the room darker and farther away; the car is roughly 1.5–3 m ahead while the nearest bins, boards, and person are about 0.5–1.5 m away. Across the five frames, the viewpoint turns right and moves toward the car and crouching person, bringing the person and foreground objects into arm’s reach by frames 4–5; the standing person in frames 1–2 is approximately 2–3 m ahead and not within reach. The car remains behind and to the right of the person, separated from them by roughly 1–2 m, while close objects along the lower edge partly occlude the floor and lower body. The map makes near/far layering clearer than RGB alone, but its absolute metric scale is uncertain, bright vertical surfaces appear spuriously close, and object boundaries around people, the car, and clutter are blurred or inconsistent.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation isolates a standing person near the center-right in frame 1 and one or two overlapping person masks near the center in frame 2, approximately 2–3 m from the camera, then isolates the car about 2–3 m ahead in frames 3–4. In frame 5 it places a crouching person low and left of the car, roughly 0.5–1 m from the camera and therefore within the camera wearer’s arm’s reach, while the car is farther back at about 1.5–2.5 m; the person faces generally toward and upward toward the camera. The masks clarify which visible regions belong to people versus the car despite clutter and partial cropping, and show the apparent rightward shift and approach across time. Reliability is limited: most shelves, tires, tools, and containers are omitted, the two frame-2 person masks may be a duplicate or fragmented detection, the frame-5 car is partly out of view, and the small “sports ball” label near the person appears inconsistent with the RGB.
descriptions.pose: The pose map detects one upright body in frame 2 about 2–3 m ahead, with the head above the torso and legs extending downward, but it provides little reliable detail about gaze or exact facing direction. It next detects the close person in frame 5 at roughly 0.5–1 m, low in the image and bent forward or crouching, with the torso angled across the frame and the head oriented approximately toward the camera; this pose is within the camera wearer’s arm’s reach. The change from an upright, farther figure to a low, close figure makes posture and relative approach clearer than RGB alone, while the car and surrounding objects remain entirely absent from this map. No poses appear in frames 1, 3, or 4 despite visible people in the RGB, limbs are incomplete, no magenta hand skeletons are shown, and the frame-5 joints are crowded and likely distorted by foreshortening and partial occlusion.
